<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par95 />feminines also: (1) a tone-lengthened vowel on the removal of the tone reverts to its original shortness (thus the ''ā'' of the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} becomes again ''ă'' in the ''construct st.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}}). On the other hand, even an originally short vowel is retained as (a long) pretonic vowel ''before'' the endings {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} in the ''abs. st.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צְדָקָה}}; (2) without the tone or foretone an originally short vowel almost always becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; on the other hand, ''before'' a vowel which had thus become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} the ''ă'' in the first syllable which had hitherto also been reduced to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} returns, although usually attenuated to ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צִדְקַת}} from ''ṣădhăqăth''; (3) in the plural of the feminines of segholate forms before the termination of {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, and in formations of the latter kind also before the light suffixes, a ''pretonic Qameṣ'' reappears, while the short vowel of the first syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}. This short vowel, however, returns in the ''construct st. plur.'', whether ending in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}; in formations of the latter kind also before the grave suffixes.

The following Paradigms (with the exception of I, ''d'') deal only with such of the forms treated in § 94 as incur some vowel changes or other. All forms with unchangeable vowels follow the analogy of Paradigm I, ''d''.
